label: Card Bank Account
title: Card Bank Account
summary: Use a Card Bank Account to summarise one linked bank account: the bank, a few facts such as the masked number, and one action.
corePrinciple: One account, a few facts, one action.

anatomy.title: The bank, its facts, and one action
anatomy.description: A white panel stacks a header with the bank’s logo, its name, and an optional badge; a list of label and value rows; and one footer button. You set them through props: institutionName, institutionAvatar, badge, items, and buttonLabel.

badge: one word about the account, such as its status.
A field name in 14 px bold; it wraps when space runs out.
The fact in 14 px, on one line.
A small Button from buttonLabel and onButtonPress, full width.
A white panel with 16 px corners and 16 by 12 px padding.

configuration.title: A badge, and the button’s colours
configuration.description: badge takes a word, which becomes a Badge in the button’s colours, or a Badge you set up yourself, such as a green status; leave it out for none. AppearanceBrand and Emphasis colour the footer button and a word badge; the defaults, Secondary at Medium emphasis, are light purple. The panel and the rows don’t change. headerSlot replaces the whole header, children replace the rows, and footer replaces the button.

states.description: The card itself isn’t pressable: the footer button is its one action, with the Button’s own hover and pressed colours. footer={false} removes it for a summary to read. The card can’t disable its button.

sizing.title: Your screen sets the width
sizing.description: The card fills its host’s width; Figma draws it at 292 px. Height follows the rows: each is 17 px, 12 px apart. The panel is padded 16 px top and bottom and 12 px at the sides, with 16 px between the header, the rows, and the button. Button / Size S, the default, is 32 px tall; M is 42 and XS 24. Avatar Size L makes the logo 42 px. List Item Style Minimal tightens the rows to 4 px apart with 12 px regular labels.

content.title: Field names and short facts
content.description: Label each row with a field name, such as Account type, and give the fact as its value. Show only the last four digits of the account number. Keep values short: a value never shrinks, so a long one squeezes its label. Label the button with a verb, such as View statement, and pass the bank’s own logo.

inContext.title: Linked accounts in Settings
inContext.description: The Bank accounts screen shows the linked account. View statement opens the screen’s own statement view through onButtonPress; the card doesn’t fetch the account or change it.

sources.title: Use the public Card Bank Account contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card / BankAccount is one 292 px component with no properties; in code it fills its host and you set it through props. Figma’s badge is amber, while the package’s takes the button’s colours (Secondary at Medium emphasis by default), and its row values are 14 px where Figma’s are 12 px. Without institutionAvatar the card shows a stock photo of a person, without other props it shows placeholder copy, and a long value squeezes its label (all reported). The published Storybook still shows the older generated page, and its Default story is gold (AppearanceBrand Primary) while the others are purple.
